title: Funerary Inscriptions, Part Two
subtitle: The Gaulish genitive — kinship, patronymics, and personal name compounds.
objectives: Recognize the genitive singular ending -i in -o- stem nouns.
Parse five inscriptions with genitive constructions.
Understand the common personal name elements: SEG-, MAR-, VER-, RIG-, DAGO-.

sections.heading: The genitive case
sections.body:
The genitive case in Gaulish marks possession and kinship. The genitive singular of -o- stem nouns (the largest class) ends in -i:

SEGOMĀROS (nominative) → SEGOMĀRI (genitive, "of Segomaros")
VILONEOS (nominative) → VILONEI (genitive, "of Viloneos")

The genitive of -ā- stem nouns (mostly feminine) ends in -as:

MĀTIR (nominative, "mother") → MĀTRAS (genitive, "of the mother")

Patronymics use the genitive: X Y-gen. = "X son of Y" or "X daughter of Y". Kinship terms follow the same pattern: X MATIR Y-gen. = "X mother of Y".

sections.heading: Inscription 1: Mother of Segomaros
sections.body:
From a funerary stone in central Gaul, 1st century CE:

MARIA SEGOMĀRI MATIR

Parsing:
MARIA — nominative singular, a Latin name ("Maria")
SEGOMĀRI — genitive singular, "of Segomaros"
MATIR — nominative singular, "mother" (cognate with Latin māter)

Translation: "Maria, mother of Segomaros."

sections.heading: Inscription 2: Son of Daxtio
sections.body:
From Alise-Sainte-Reine, 1st century CE:

ATEPOMĀROS DAXTIONI

Parsing:
ATEPOMĀROS — nominative singular, "very great"
DAXTIONI — genitive singular, "of Daxtio" (the ending -oni is a variant genitive for -on- stem nouns)

Translation: "Atepomaros son of Daxtio."

sections.heading: Inscription 3: Daughter of Dannotalos
sections.body:
From Autun, 1st century CE:

PRISCA DANNOTALI

Parsing:
PRISCA — nominative singular, a Latin name ("Prisca")
DANNOTALI — genitive singular, "of Dannotalos"

Translation: "Prisca daughter of Dannotalos."

sections.heading: Inscription 4: Wife of Eporedorix
sections.body:
From Saint-Marcel, 1st century CE:

SEVERA EPOREDORIGI GNATHA

Parsing:
SEVERA — nominative singular, a Latin name ("Severa")
EPOREDORIGI — genitive singular, "of Eporedorix"
GNATHA — nominative singular, "wife" or "daughter" (cognate with Latin nata, "born")

Translation: "Severa, wife of Eporedorix."

sections.heading: Name elements and meanings
sections.body:
Gaulish personal names are transparent compounds. The most common elements:

SEG- (victory) — SEGOMĀROS ("great in victory")
MAR- (great) — appears in SEGOMĀROS, ATEPOMAROS, NERTOMAROS
VER- (over, super-) — VERCINGETORIX ("king over warriors")
RIG-, -RIX (king) — EPOREDORIX, DVBNORIX, VERCINGETORIX
DAGO- (good) — DAGOMĀROS ("good and great")
BRIG- (high) — BRIGOMAGLOS ("high prince")
NERT- (strength) — NERTOMAROS ("great in strength")
EPO- (horse) — EPOREDORIX ("horse-driving king")

Learn these elements and you can parse any Gaulish name.
